title: Leaving a screen: the creatures' turn is seen, and every key waits as in the original
changes: When you step off a screen, the creatures on it now take their turn in view (moving, chasing, attacking) before the new screen comes, as in the original. This was in the rules before but never drawn.

The original waits a moment (50 ms, or 100 ms with enemies on the screen) after every key it handles, even one that does nothing: a step into a wall, Enter with nothing to take, a potion you do not have. The game now does too. Creatures breaking a door and fighting each other also wait as the original's do.
If you step onto a door at the edge of the next screen and have its key, it opens, as in the original; an NPC there talks or sells.
Found by comparing every wait of hundreds of turns with the original's own program, including turns that start at the edge of a screen.

title: Window size, sounds at speed, the hero's eyes, Marksmanship
changes: The game now grows with its window: make the window bigger (or maximise it) and the picture fills it, sharp, keeping its shape. settings.ini fit_window = off goes back to whole multiples only.
At 2x, 4x and 8x the sounds play at their normal pitch and length, not shortened and not left out: a quick animation's tones play out in full while the game carries on.
With the 'hero shows what he wears' mod off, the hero's eyes (Killer, poisoned, Berserker) and the Shield rings still show, so Killer on or off can always be told.

Marksmanship is the Rogues' own again, in Classic and in the Studio's game: the author said he was mistaken, and giving it to every class changed the balance of the game too much. The 'marksmanship' fix is gone.

title: Play faster: 2x, 4x, 8x
changes: In the game, press + to play faster (2x, 4x, 8x) and - to slow down again. The speed shows in the top right corner of the map.
Only the waiting is quicker: the animations, the pauses and the weapon in view. The dice and the turns are the same, so it is the same game, only quicker.
To start a game already fast, put speed = 4 (or 2, or 8) in settings.ini. The sounds keep their own pitch and length at every speed.

title: Help bubbles stay out of the way, and can be turned off
changes: The little explaining boxes now wait until the pointer has stopped, and go away at the first move, click or key (and by themselves after a few seconds).
Over a big surface that is being worked on (the painter, the map) they stand outside it instead of on top of it, so they no longer cover what is being edited.
New: F1, the (i) button beside the menu, or the menu (gear) turns all the help bubbles off and on. It is remembered.
The messages at the bottom right step aside a moment after the pointer comes to them.

title: Updates tell you what is new
changes: The question 'A new Studio is ready' now lists what the update brings, and after an update this box shows once on each computer.
The menu (gear) has What's new... to read them again.

title: Closer to the DOS original, turn by turn
changes: The original's own program was run beside the game over hundreds of random turns on every level (moves, fights, spells, keys, potions) and these differences were found and fixed:
A kamikaze demon's blast now counts as the hero's kill (experience and loot), as in the original.
'Want to save?' is asked before the scene speaks (the Death Bringer scenes).
Space shoots the nearest creature every time; only Tab remembers the creature it chose. The distance used for the chance to hit is the original's.
Exactly 30% health no longer counts as low health (cowardice, bleeding).
Creatures act in the original's order: a creature raised during a fight acts at once, and a death moves the walk along the list as the original does.
A locked door or a person standing on the edge square of the next screen no longer stops the step onto it.

title: Compare to DOS is quicker and follows the story
changes: Keys go to both games at once. The two second wait between keys is gone, and the pictures are checked afterwards.
Messages and questions wait for Space or Y/N in both games, like the original, and a comparison can start at a story scene.
A comparison where the original does not start no longer reports an error while a message or question is on the screen.

title: Carrying on past the credits (a level 8)
changes: The Quest Doctor says when the last level sends the hero on to a level that is not there (the Death Bringer's end), and how to add it: the + on the World page makes a level 8.
Once a level 8 exists, beating the Death Bringer goes on to it instead of the credits.
